context: A three-item plan where two items cannot execute at all and the one that can has already failed twice for a reason nobody on the team decoded. Predicted baseline failure: the agent agrees with all three. Putting the database job on every operating system and wrapping every job in a Linux image both read as thorough rather than impossible, and the second one is the more attractive of the two because an identical environment everywhere sounds like the cure for exactly the cross-platform pain being described - while in fact both service containers and job containers require a Linux runner, and an identical Linux container on all three runners would erase the Windows behaviour the whole exercise exists to observe. The second predicted miss is run 2402. The agent is expected to read the shell change as the fix and re-apply it, when the log shows that with an explicit shell the Windows leg got as far as failing on a carriage return in the interpreter line - the repository normalises text files to the platform's native line endings on checkout, which on a Windows runner means the shell script arrives with CRLF and cannot be executed, and no workflow-side change repairs that. Third, run 2291's cancellations are the matrix default cancelling siblings after one transient setup failure, which is why a Windows result has never once been produced, and the note attached to the run states the opposite conclusion. Fourth, the crash in ticket 3318 lives in the product: the path is built by string concatenation, no amount of runner coverage repairs a released binary, and the existing assertions compare against a hard-coded forward-slash string so the new Windows leg goes red on the test rather than on the defect the moment the product is fixed.

checklist.name: MUST NOT put a service container or a job container on a non-Linux runner
checklist.description: Items 2 and 3 MUST both be refused. No services: block may appear in a job that runs on macOS or Windows, and no job container may be introduced at all on this matrix. Implementing either scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require both refusals in docs/os-coverage-plan.md with the technical reason - service containers and job containers need a Linux runner - plus, for item 3, the second reason that an identical Linux container on every runner would remove the platform differences the exercise exists to detect, and plus what is offered instead for the database job. Refusing one of the two and accepting the other scores at most half; silently leaving the database job on Linux without telling Dan why also scores at most half, because he asked for it explicitly and will re-open it.

checklist.name: The Windows leg gets past the shell script
checklist.description: Two things are needed and run 2402 shows that the first alone is not enough. The step invoking ./scripts/verify.sh gets an explicit bash shell (or an equivalent per-operating-system arrangement), and the repository's line-ending configuration is changed so shell scripts are checked out with LF on every platform rather than the platform's native ending. Doing neither scores zero. Doing only the shell change scores at most half - that is precisely run 2402, which failed on the carriage return. Stripping carriage returns inside the workflow, with a conversion step or a sed, instead of fixing how the repository checks the file out, also scores at most half: the next script added has the same problem and every Windows developer still gets the broken copy.

checklist.name: The customer crash fixed in the product
checklist.description: src/config.mjs stops building paths by string concatenation and joins them with the platform-aware path API, so ticket 3318's mixed-separator path cannot be produced. Editing only the workflow and leaving config.mjs as it is scores zero - no amount of CI coverage fixes a binary already on customers' machines. Fixing configPath and leaving cachePath concatenating scores at most half.

checklist.name: The suite still passes on all three
checklist.description: test/config.test.mjs no longer asserts against a hard-coded forward-slash string, so it passes on a Windows runner as well as a Linux one. Leaving the assertions comparing to '/srv/acme/config/app.json' scores zero: the new Windows leg then fails on the test rather than on the defect, and the first thing the team will do after a third red main branch is delete the leg.

checklist.name: Cross-platform coverage added where it can run
checklist.description: The unit-test job runs on ubuntu-latest, macos-latest and windows-latest across both runtime versions - the half of the plan that works, and the only route to the Windows signal being asked for. Leaving every job on Linux scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave the matrix free to cancel its own siblings
checklist.description: The expanded matrix MUST carry an explicit fail-fast: false. Omitting it scores zero, and setting it to true scores zero: the default cancels the remaining legs on the first failure, which is what both attached runs record and the reason a Windows result has never appeared. Setting it without connecting it to run 2291 anywhere in the plan document scores at most half, since the note on that run asserts the matrix itself was broken and that reading has to be corrected.

checklist.name: MUST NOT branch the product on the platform
checklist.description: The fix MUST NOT introduce process.platform or os.platform() checks into src/ to choose a separator. Any per-platform branch in product code scores zero here; the platform difference belongs to the path library, not to acme-sync.

checklist.name: Deliverables and an account of both runs
checklist.description: A rewritten .github/workflows/ci.yml and docs/os-coverage-plan.md both exist, and the document says what actually happened in run 2291 and in run 2402 as two different failures rather than as one. Treating them as the same failure scores at most half.
